propositions: Pandoc subprocess invocations can hang indefinitely (observed 13.5 min at 95.8% CPU) because pypandoc provides no timeout and subprocess.run(timeout=) reaps only the direct child, allowing CPU-spinning grandchildren to survive.

The DC renderer must use caller-side wall-clock timeout via proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s) with process group reaping via rebar._proc.reap_process_group to kill spinning descendant processes on timeout.
The timeout is a config key (reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s, default 10s) reachable from config files and environment variables.
Per-unit fallback to original Markdown on timeout or non-zero exit must remain unchanged; one unit's failure does not affect another.
Pandoc GPL licence and wheel-bundled binary provenance must be recorded in a repo-root NOTICE file and the pypandoc-binary version pin verified in CI.
Rendered output must remain byte-identical to the landed renderer across the full 178-body corpus, proving this change addresses robustness only, not rendering semantics.
